feat(audit): Add CSV export of the audit log

Enterprise customers' compliance teams import the audit log into a
spreadsheet every quarter. The JSON export is hard to read in that
format, so the CSV export gives them a file they can open directly.

The new /audit.csv route writes a header row (ts, actor, action) and
then one row per log entry. It streams the rows as it reads them, so
memory use stays flat even for logs with millions of entries.

fix(pay): Retry failed charges and wait for gateway in test

Charge sends the card to the payment gateway once, so a single failed
call fails the whole checkout. Charge now retries the gateway call up
to three times and returns the first success, or the last error if
every attempt fails.

TestCharge waited a fixed 10 ms for the gateway to come up. When the
test environment was slow, the gateway was not ready in time and the
test failed intermittently. The test now waits until the gateway
reports ready, so it no longer depends on timing.

perf(search): Load result rows with one query

The search page loaded each result row with its own database query, so
one request cost a round trip per row on the page. The 95th percentile
latency of the page grew with the number of rows.

load() now fetches every requested item in one query that matches the
full list of IDs. The database does the lookup in a single round trip.

Rows come back in database order, not in the order of the IDs passed
in. An ID with no matching item adds no row to the result.

perf(search): Fetch search result rows in one query

The search page ran one query per result row to load the items, so each
page paid a round trip for every row. At the 95th percentile the page took
2.4 seconds. load now fetches all rows for the requested ids in a single
query with `id = any(...)`, which brought the page to about 300 ms.

The rows come back in no particular order. Callers must not rely on the
order of the ids they passed in.

perf(search): Load result rows in one query

The search page loaded each result with its own query, so one page cost one round trip per row (the N+1 problem). At the 95th percentile the page took 2.4 seconds. load() now sends all ids in one query, `id = any(%s)`, and the page takes about 300 ms at the same percentile.

The old loop returned one entry per id, in id order. The new query returns the matching rows in database order, so a caller that needs the order of ids must sort the result itself.

perf(search): Load result rows with one query

The search page ran one database query per result row, which is the
N+1 query problem. At the 95th percentile, the page took 2.4 seconds.

The results loader now fetches all requested items in one query that
matches on the list of ids. At the 95th percentile, the page now takes
about 300 ms.

Rows come back in database order, not in the order of ids. Ids with no
matching row are left out of the result instead of appearing as None.

perf(search): Load result rows in one query

The search page ran one database query per result row. The number of
queries grew with the page size, and the page responded slowly as a
result. Load all rows for the requested ids with a single query instead.

The query returns only ids that exist. Before, a missing id produced
None in the list. The result also no longer follows the order of ids.
Callers that depend on either behavior must change.

test(cart): Cover rejection of expired coupons

No test checked that an expired coupon is refused. Bug #412 let expired
coupons apply to a cart, and the existing tests did not catch it.

TestExpiredCouponIsRejected builds a coupon that expired an hour ago and
expects Apply to return an error.
